title: Never Look Too Interested

pre.en: How much did Chen pay for the clock in the end?
pre.zh: 小陈最后花多少钱买下了那个钟？

intro: 一段对话：Tom 带小陈逛约克的 Shambles 市场，教他怎么讲价，小陈看上了一个老式黄铜钟。读的时候留意一般过去时的被动：卖家讲钟的来历时说 It was made …、it was found …，要说是谁做的，就加 by。

sentences.en: Right, welcome to Shambles Market.
sentences.zh: 好了，欢迎来到 Shambles 市场。
sentences.speaker: Tom

sentences.en: Rule one: never look too interested.
sentences.zh: 第一条规矩：千万别显得太想要。

sentences.en: In a supermarket, the price is the price, but at a market stall, nothing is sold at the first price.
sentences.zh: 在超市，标多少就是多少；可在市场的摊位上，没有东西是按开价卖的。

sentences.en: I've seen this place on Instagram, but it's much busier in person.
sentences.zh: 我在 Instagram 上见过这地方，不过亲眼看比照片上热闹多了。
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: Anyway, I'm out of the office until next Monday, so I've got all week to practise.
sentences.zh: 反正我下周一之前都不用上班，有一整个星期可以练。

sentences.en: Rule two: don't ask what something costs.
sentences.zh: 第二条：别问东西多少钱。
sentences.speaker: Tom

sentences.en: Ask what they want for it.
And rule three: never accept the first price.
sentences.zh: 第三条：开价绝对不能接。

sentences.en: At least pretend to think about it for a while.
sentences.zh: 至少也要装模作样想一会儿。

sentences.en: Oh wow, look at that brass clock!
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: It's just like the one on the platform at York station!
sentences.zh: 跟约克火车站站台上那个一模一样！

sentences.en: Chen.
sentences.speaker: Tom

sentences.en: What did I just say about rule one?
sentences.zh: 我刚说的第一条是什么来着？

sentences.en: Morning! Feel free to pick it up.
sentences.speaker: Seller

sentences.en: It was made in Sheffield in 1920, and it was found in a farmhouse near Whitby.
sentences.zh: 它是 1920 年在谢菲尔德造的，是在惠特比附近的一座农舍里找到的。

sentences.en: My wife wants me to get rid of it before Christmas.
sentences.zh: 我老婆想让我圣诞节前把它处理掉。

sentences.en: Hmm, it's all right, I suppose.
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: How much do you want for it?
For you, forty pounds.
sentences.speaker: Seller

sentences.en: And that's me being generous.
Forty? That's a rip-off.
sentences.speaker: Tom

sentences.en: If I were you, I'd offer twenty-five.
I heard that, young man.
sentences.speaker: Seller

sentences.en: It was cleaned by my daughter last week, you know.
sentences.zh: 这可是我女儿上周刚擦干净的。

sentences.en: Look, I'll meet you halfway.
Thirty-two pounds, take it or leave it.
Deal!
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: Not bad for your first try.
sentences.speaker: Tom

sentences.en: You knocked eight pounds off.
And for a clock that old, thirty-two pounds is a bargain.
sentences.zh: 这么老的钟，32 英镑算捡了个便宜。

sentences.en: Now let's grab a bite and buy Mum's pickle.
sentences.zh: 走，先随便吃点，再给我妈买罐酱。

sentences.en: We're already behind schedule.
Wait.
sentences.speaker: Chen

sentences.en: There's a tiny sticker on the bottom.
It says, "Made in Shenzhen, 2019."
Well, it was made by experts.
sentences.speaker: Tom

cards.note: 摆摊的人叫 stallholder；market stall、food stall 都很常见。
if you do something in person, you go somewhere or meet someone yourself, not by phone or online

cards.zh: 不在办公室；外出（不上班）
cards.note: to be away from work, for example on holiday or at an appointment
cards.tip: 邮件自动回复就叫 out-of-office reply；常说到哪天：until Monday。
cards.example: I'll be out of the office on Friday, so please email Rachel.

cards.note: used to say that a bad situation has one good point; not less than
后面接 to do 或 that 从句：pretend to be busy / pretend that you're busy。
放在名词前当形容词用：a brass clock、brass buttons。
used to tell someone that they can do something if they want to
cards.tip: 后面接动词原形；比 You can … 更热情、更客气。
cards.example: Feel free to call me if you have any questions.

cards.note: farm + house；英国乡下很多老农舍有几百年历史。
to throw away, sell or give away something you do not want

cards.text: how much do you want for sth?
cards.note: a question you ask a seller when you want to know the price and maybe pay less
cards.tip: 比 How much is it? 多一层「价钱可以谈」的意思，在市场、二手买卖里常用；问的是卖家心里的价。
cards.example: How much do you want for the bike? It looks a bit old.

cards.note: something that costs much more than it should
cards.tip: 口语，常说 That's a rip-off 或 What a rip-off!；动词说法是 rip sb off（宰某人）。
cards.example: Eight pounds for a coffee? That's a rip-off.

cards.note: to agree to some of what another person wants so that you can both agree
cards.tip: 不只用于讲价，开会、商量计划都能用；meet halfway 是双方各退一步，不是只有一方让。
cards.example: You want Friday and I want Monday, so let's meet halfway and say Wednesday.

cards.note: 也能放在名词前：the halfway point（中点）；halfway through the film 电影看到一半。
said when you will not change an offer and the other person must accept it or refuse it
cards.tip: 语气很硬，是在说「不再让价了」；对上司、客户说会显得没礼貌。
cards.example: This is my last offer — take it or leave it.

cards.note: to take an amount away from a price
cards.tip: 钱数放在中间：knock £5 off；也可以说 knock £5 off the price。
cards.example: The shop knocked ten pounds off because the box was damaged.

cards.note: to be sold for less than its real value
cards.tip: bargain 是名词，前面要有 a：It's a bargain；不说 It's very bargain。
cards.example: These boots were a bargain — I paid half the normal price.

cards.tip: 口语；完整一点说 grab a bite to eat。
cards.example: Do you want to grab a bite after the meeting?

cards.note: 动词 stick 是「粘贴」；price sticker 价格标签。
